To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a LTV-MP C controller that is based on linearizations of the vehicle dynamics that are adapted over the prediction horizon, can achieve a higher control performance than a LTV-M PC controller that uses linearization of the vehicle dynamics which remain unchanged over the horizon.

a linear time-vARYing model-based predictive control (LTV-M PC) controller can be used to achieve a good control performance at the limit of the vehicle dynamics, if the controller employs estimations of state variables and control inputs to perform successive linearizations of the model over the prediction time.

a LTV-MPCC for lateral vehicle guidance at the limits of the vehicle dynamics can be achieved by using estimations of the steering angle and the state variable trajectory for successive linearization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a LTV-Mpc controller for lateral vehicle guidance that is able to provide an improved control performance at the vehicle dynamics limit.
the design of a LTV-Mpc controller for vehicle guidance that is suitable for collision avoidance systems.

the design of a LTV-MC controller for the lateral vehicle guidance by means of front steering at the limit of the vehicle dynamics, which can be used in the scope of an integrated collision avoidance system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the estimation based approach is superior to the approach without estimation.
the estimation-based LTV-MPC approach can be used to improve the performance of the controller.
this approach is a suitable solution to achieve an improved control performance at the dynamic vehicle limits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a LTV-MP controller that is based on a nonlinear model and that uses estimations of the state variable trajectory and the applied steering angle can achieve a higher control performance compared to a LTI-MPC controller that is based upon a linear model and that uses constant linearizations of the prediction model.
the proposed LTV-MPC approach is able to provide an improved control performance at the limit of vehicle dynamics.
the estimation-based LTV-MPC approach can be used to improve the control performance at the vehicle limits of lateral dynamics, which is a crucial requirement for a collision avoidance system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a linearization based on the state variable trajectory is more suitable to describe the nonlinear behavior of the vehicle than the linearization based on an estimation of the applied steering input.
the estimation-based approach is able to provide a better performance at the limits.
the proposed approach is a viable alternative to the state of the art for lateral vehicle control at the limits of its dynamics.
